newsitem.title: JAPAN: LDP official nixes help for big debenture holders.
newsitem.headline: LDP official nixes help for big debenture holders.

text.p: A senior politician of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) said companies and financial institutions holding bank debentures should not receive protection from government funds.
"Depositors to be protected with public money are ordinary depositors," LDP policy chief Taku Yamasaki told a television programme on Sunday.

Yamasaki said he personally thought corporations and financial institutions holding debentures issued by long-term credit banks should have to deal with the situation themselves if the banks became insolvent.

Some analysts said on Monday they were surprised by Yamasaki's remarks, which came after the rating on bank debentures issued by one of Japan's three long-term credit banks, Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, was cut to junk bond levels by an international rating agency.

Moody's Investors Service said on Friday it had cut the rating of NCB debentures to Ba1 from Baa3 as it expected NCB might ultimately need outside assistance because of "substantial unrealised losses" in its loan portfolio.
Such a rating puts the debentures below investment grade, commonly known as junk bond status.
